lesson.title: Finding Zeros of Polynomial Functions
intro: The zeros of a polynomial are the \(x\)-values that make the function equal to zero.
If a polynomial is written in factored form, set each factor equal to zero.
A zero corresponds to an \(x\)-intercept on the graph.
Carefully solve each factor to find all zeros.

steps: Set each factor equal to zero.
workedExample.aiHint: In factored form, each factor gives one possible zero.

questions.prompt: The zeros of the function \(f(x)=x(x-5)(3x+6)\) are
questions.explanation: Set each factor equal to zero: \(x=0\), \(x-5=0\Rightarrow x=5\), and \(3x+6=0\Rightarrow x=-2\).

questions.prompt: Which function has the zeros \(-1\), 3, and \(-4\)?
questions.explanation: A zero at -1 gives factor \((x+1)\), a zero at 3 gives factor \((x-3)\), and a zero at -4 gives factor \((x+4)\).
